messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: serving-runtime pool-7 reporting repeated warmup failures and elevated OOMs. Auto-page to #incidents and oncall.
jun: seeing huge spike in warmup failures across pool-7. Logs show OOM during model deserialization and then compile timeouts. paging samir (eng-runtime) and lia (eng-sre).
samir: on it. grabbing logs now. any recent deploys to pool-7? alex, did we push any model artifacts in the last 30m?
alex: no deploys from me in last hour. only automated artifact promotion earlier today. I can rollback to artifact v20260214 if needed.
lia: rolling nodes 7a/7b/7c are flapping — kube shows repeated container crashes and restart loops. suspect bad artifact or corrupted tarball during pull.
jun: pasted a sample of the deserialize failure:
```
ERROR: model_warmup: failed to deserialize weights for model: redwood-ggml-13b
Caused by: checksum mismatch while reading shard 3
Stack: RuntimeError: deserialization failed, aborting warmup
```
jun: and a CUDA OOM from same timeframe:
```
E 03:12:45 cuda_ops.cpp:92 CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 1.2 GiB
E 03:12:45 runtime_warmup.cpp:341 warmup failed: cuda OOM
```
samir: those two together explain it — corrupted artifact triggers a larger-than-expected memcpy pattern, then kernel compile cache triggering extra allocations -> OOM. also seeing repeated compile timeouts:
```
W 03:13:02 kernel_builder.cpp:201 compile timeout after 120s for aten_conv2d
```
lia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon pool-7 nodes to stop new warmups 2) scale down warmup concurrency on all pools 3) restore previous artifact from s3 and restart warmup on a single canary node 4) extend compile timeout to 300s temporarily
jun: commands i'm running now:
```
kubectl cordon node/pool-7-a
kubectl patch ds warmup-daemon -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"warmup","env":[{"name":"WARMUP_CONCURRENCY","value":"1"}]}]}}}}'
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/models/redwood-ggml-13b/v20260214/ /var/tmp/ggml --recursive
```
alex: deploy-bot initiated artifact rollback to v20260214 on pool-7 canary node. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollback started for artifact redwood-ggml-13b -> v20260214. will post status updates.
maria: tapping CS now. asking which customers saw errors and pulling metrics (error rate, 5xxs, latency). will prepare an outbound.
jun: initial customer impact — Metrics show error rate spike ~03:12–03:24 UTC, affected ~3 high-traffic tenants. Latency for those tenants spiked to 2-3x for remaining requests. No data exfiltration detected.
lia: I've cordoned nodes and scaled warmup concurrency. canary warmup using v20260214 is running, logs look healthy so far.
samir: added temporary mitigation to runtime config: increase compile timeout to 300s and enable fallback-to-quantized-variant if warmup fails. pushing config now.
samir: confirmed compile cache invalidation also happening — we need to fix durability of compile cache on restart; opened PR #1258 but not part of immediate mitigation.
jun: lia, once canary finishes warmup, please uncordon and roll rest of pool-7 with the restored artifact. avoid parallel warmups >2 concurrently.
lia: ack. rolling in controlled batches. monitoring OOM metrics and container restarts.
alex: postmortem note: artifact upload job did not complete checksum validation on shard 3 due to transient S3 error. adding extra verification step to CI.
maria: CS notified the 3 impacted customers, offering credits and a summary once we have a final RCA. one customer already replied asking for ETA — I gave conservative 90m.
deploy-bot: rollback completed on canary. warmup succeeded. starting rolling restart according to strategy.
jun: handing off to samir for overnight monitoring. samir, if anything degrades please escalate to oncall SRE.
samir: will monitor for 2h and then hand to next oncall. leaving a short runbook note in the incident doc: 1) check warmup OOMs, 2) check deserialize checksum alerts, 3) confirm compile cache health.
lia: incident-timestamped notes added to #incidents-log. tagging for postmortem and compliance.
jun: TL;DR: root cause = corrupted artifact shard causing deserialization failures -> unexpected memory patterns -> CUDA OOMs and compile timeouts -> container crashes and node flaps. Mitigation = rollback to known-good artifact, reduce concurrency, extend compile timeout, enable fallback variant, coordinate controlled roll. Customer impact limited to 3 tenants, CS notified.
maria: thanks team. follow-up actions assigned: alex -> CI artifact validation; samir -> compile cache durability fix; lia -> warmup throttling defaults; jun -> write initial incident timeline & RCA draft.
jun: closing thread here, will link final incident doc when RCA is ready. :white_check_mark:
